The opinion expressly frames the dog-sniff question through legitimate privacy interests and constitutionally protected privacy.
The text states that conduct revealing only contraband compromises no legitimate privacy interest and contrasts privacy society is prepared to consider reasonable.
residual_risks: Home-role labels are editorial taxonomy, but the disclosed opinion text supports this related cross-doctrine placement.

reasons: The granted question was whether reasonable suspicion is required for a drug-detection dog sniff during a legitimate traffic stop.
The holding and analysis turn on whether the sniff prolonged or changed the character of a lawful traffic stop.
residual_risks: Key/anchor status is editorial, but the case is centrally about traffic-stop dog sniffs.

defect.evidence_quote: A dog sniff conducted during a concededly lawful traffic stop that reveals no information other than the location of a substance that no individual has any right to possess does not violate the Fourth Amendment.
defect.problem: The holding is directionally supported but slightly overbroad because it says a dog sniff reveals only contraband without the opinion's qualifiers: a well-trained narcotics-detection dog/properly conducted sniff and a sniff revealing no information other than contraband.
defect.proposed_fix: A well-trained narcotics-detection dog sniff of a vehicle's exterior during a lawful traffic stop, when it does not prolong the stop and reveals no information other than contraband, requires no independent reasonable suspicion and does not violate the Fourth Amendment.

reasons: The no-suspicion point follows from the stated question and the Court's assumption that the officer conducting the sniff had no information about respondent beyond the speeding stop.
The opinion also states that use of a well-trained narcotics-detection dog during a lawful traffic stop generally does not implicate legitimate privacy interests.
residual_risks: No separate lake holding field was provided, so support was checked against the cached opinion text and pinpoints.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add well-trained narcotics-detection dog and no-information-other-than-contraband qualifiers.
